# Data Source: stripe_terminal_configuration

How Stripe Terminal readers behave: tipping, splash screens, reboot window and Wi-Fi.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_terminal_configuration" "store" {
  id = stripe_terminal_configuration.store.id
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the terminal configuration to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `bbpos_wisepad3` - An object containing device type specific settings for BBPOS WisePad 3 readers. See [`bbpos_wisepad3`](#bbpos_wisepad3) below.
* `bbpos_wisepos_e` - An object containing device type specific settings for BBPOS WisePOS E readers. See [`bbpos_wisepos_e`](#bbpos_wisepos_e) below.
* `cellular` - Configuration for cellular connectivity. See [`cellular`](#cellular) below.
* `is_account_default` - Whether this Configuration is the default for your account
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `name` - Name of the configuration
* `offline` - Configurations for collecting transactions offline. See [`offline`](#offline) below.
* `reboot_window` - Reboot time settings for readers. that support customized reboot time configuration. See [`reboot_window`](#reboot_window) below.
* `stripe_s700` - An object containing device type specific settings for Stripe S700 readers. See [`stripe_s700`](#stripe_s700) below.
* `stripe_s710` - An object containing device type specific settings for Stripe S710 readers. See [`stripe_s710`](#stripe_s710) below.
* `tipping` - Tipping configurations for readers that support on-reader tips. See [`tipping`](#tipping) below.
* `verifone_m425` - An object containing device type specific settings for Verifone M425 readers. See [`verifone_m425`](#verifone_m425) below.
* `verifone_p400` - An object containing device type specific settings for Verifone P400 readers. See [`verifone_p400`](#verifone_p400) below.
* `verifone_p630` - An object containing device type specific settings for Verifone P630 readers. See [`verifone_p630`](#verifone_p630) below.
* `verifone_ux700` - An object containing device type specific settings for Verifone UX700 readers. See [`verifone_ux700`](#verifone_ux700) below.
* `verifone_v660p` - An object containing device type specific settings for Verifone V660p readers. See [`verifone_v660p`](#verifone_v660p) below.
* `wifi` - Configurations for connecting to a WiFi network. See [`wifi`](#wifi) below.

<a id="bbpos_wisepad3"></a>
### `bbpos_wisepad3`

The `bbpos_wisepad3` attribute supports:

* `splashscreen` - A File ID representing an image to display on the reader

<a id="bbpos_wisepos_e"></a>
### `bbpos_wisepos_e`

The `bbpos_wisepos_e` attribute supports:

* `splashscreen` - A File ID representing an image to display on the reader

<a id="cellular"></a>
### `cellular`

The `cellular` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Whether a cellular-capable reader can connect to the internet over cellular.

<a id="offline"></a>
### `offline`

The `offline` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Determines whether to allow transactions to be collected while reader is offline. Defaults to false.

<a id="reboot_window"></a>
### `reboot_window`

The `reboot_window` attribute supports:

* `end_hour` - Integer between 0 to 23 that represents the end hour of the reboot time window. The value must be different than the start_hour.
* `start_hour` - Integer between 0 to 23 that represents the start hour of the reboot time window.

<a id="tipping.aed"></a>
### `tipping.aed`

The `tipping.aed` attribute supports:

* `fixed_amounts` - Fixed amounts displayed when collecting a tip
* `percentages` - Percentages displayed when collecting a tip
* `smart_tip_threshold` - Below this amount, fixed amounts will be displayed; above it, percentages will be displayed

<a id="wifi"></a>
### `wifi`

The `wifi` attribute supports:

* `enterprise_eap_peap` - See [`wifi.enterprise_eap_peap`](#wifi.enterprise_eap_peap) below.
* `enterprise_eap_tls` - See [`wifi.enterprise_eap_tls`](#wifi.enterprise_eap_tls) below.
* `personal_psk` - See [`wifi.personal_psk`](#wifi.personal_psk) below.
* `type` - Security type of the WiFi network. The hash with the corresponding name contains the credentials for this security type. Possible values: `enterprise_eap_peap`, `enterprise_eap_tls`, `personal_psk`.

<a id="wifi.enterprise_eap_peap"></a>
### `wifi.enterprise_eap_peap`

The `wifi.enterprise_eap_peap` attribute supports:

* `ca_certificate_file` - A File ID representing a PEM file containing the server certificate
* `password` - (Sensitive) Password for connecting to the WiFi network
* `ssid` - Name of the WiFi network
* `username` - Username for connecting to the WiFi network

<a id="wifi.enterprise_eap_tls"></a>
### `wifi.enterprise_eap_tls`

The `wifi.enterprise_eap_tls` attribute supports:

* `ca_certificate_file` - A File ID representing a PEM file containing the server certificate
* `client_certificate_file` - A File ID representing a PEM file containing the client certificate
* `private_key_file` - A File ID representing a PEM file containing the client RSA private key
* `private_key_file_password` - (Sensitive) Password for the private key file
* `ssid` - Name of the WiFi network

<a id="wifi.personal_psk"></a>
### `wifi.personal_psk`

The `wifi.personal_psk` attribute supports:

* `password` - (Sensitive) Password for connecting to the WiFi network
* `ssid` - Name of the WiFi network
